predecessors.name: Duchy of Livonia
predecessors.text: Livonia north of Latgale without Ösel: Vidzeme, Riga and southern Estonia

predecessors.name: Denmark-Norway
predecessors.text: the island of Ösel (Saaremaa), which Denmark ceded to Sweden at Brömsebro

successors.name: Tsardom of Russia
successors.text: Riga Governorate: the Livonian nobility and Riga capitulated on 4/15 July 1710, Pernau in August 1710; the Treaty of Nystad (30 August 1721) made the cession formal

ledger.x: August 1621: the Swedish invasion of Livonia begins; the siege of Riga opened on 29 August.
25 September 1621: Riga capitulates to Gustavus Adolphus and Swedish Livonia begins.
January 1622: Valmiera (Wolmar) and several smaller Livonian castles fall to the Swedes.
1625: Koknese falls after a sixteen-day siege (the Swedes landed in June 1625).
27 August 1625: Dorpat (Tartu) falls to the Swedes.
25 September 1629: the Truce of Altmark recognises Sweden's conquest of most of the Duchy of Livonia.
25 September 1629: the Truce of Altmark ends the fighting for Livonia; the Commonwealth keeps the Inflanty Voivodeship.
13 August 1645: the Treaty of Brömsebro gives Sweden the island of Ösel.
23 April 1660: the Treaty of Oliva formally cedes Livonia to Sweden; the page: 'the whole territory was formally ceded'.
March 1700: Augustus II's Saxon forces invade Swedish Livonia and besiege Riga.
June 1701: Charles XII defeats the Saxons and Russians at the Düna crossing and then Augustus at Riga; the siege is over.
4/15 July 1710: Riga and the Livonian nobility capitulate to Russia.
1710: Ösel passes to Russia with the rest of Livonia.

wars.name: Polish-Swedish War (1621-1625)
wars.outcome: Sweden took Riga (25 September 1621), Valmiera (January 1622), Koknese and Dorpat (1625) and kept Livonia north of the Daugava; the Truce of Altmark (25 September 1629) recognised the gains.

wars.name: Torstenson War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Brömsebro, 13 August 1645: Denmark-Norway ceded Ösel and Gotland, Jämtland and Härjedalen, and Halland for thirty years.

wars.name: Great Northern War
wars.outcome: Russia captured Riga and Tallinn in 1710 and 'evicted Sweden from the Baltic provinces'; the Treaty of Nystad (30 August 1721 O.S.) gave Russia Estonia, Livonia, Ingria and Kexholm.

certainty.note: Shapes follow modern county and commune names; the Latgale (Inflanty) line of 1629 is the truce line but the page names only the region.
